children: Stocks kicked off the week on an upbeat note, bolstered by falling oil prices and optimism around this week's talks between Washington and Beijing.

The Nasdaq is leading the gains, rising about 2%, thanks to a rally in chip makers and other AI-related stocks. Yesterday, AI was a major focus of talks in New York between American and Chinese officials ahead of Chinese leader Xi Jinping's visit to the U.S. later this week. One topic discussed, according to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent: a "notification mechanism" for AI incidents that could affect national security.

Falling oil prices are also adding to the upbeat tone this morning. Brent crude futures are down about 4% to trade below $100 a barrel, on track for a fourth straight day of losses. That's helping send global bond yields lower on both sides of the Atlantic. The 10-year yield is trading around 4.97%.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
